episode.content: Every receipt in expense claim EC-0419 is dated within its 1–15 October claim period.
episode.evidence:
One receipt in EC-0419 is dated outside the 1-15 October claim period, so the claim that every receipt falls within it is false.

The record states receipt dates are DD/MM/YYYY as printed. Against a 1-15 October period inclusive:
  R1 02/10/2026 = 2 Oct  - within
  R2 03/10/2026 = 3 Oct  - within
  R3 06/10/2026 = 6 Oct  - within
  R4 09/10/2026 = 9 Oct  - within
  R5 11/10/2026 = 11 Oct - within
  R6 14/10/2026 = 14 Oct - within
  R7 17/10/2026 = 17 Oct - OUTSIDE the period (period closes 15 October)

R7 (taxi, station to client site, 21.30) is two days after the period end. The claim is universal ('every receipt'), so a single out-of-period receipt defeats it; this is not a matter of degree or of the proportion of compliant receipts.

The date format does not rescue R7: a month-first reading is impossible because 17 is not a valid month, and it would in any case move the other receipts outside the period too.

The amounts are not in issue and I do not dispute them: 86.40 + 112.00 + 47.85 + 14.50 + 38.99 + 54.10 + 21.30 = 375.14, matching the total claimed. The in-period subtotal is 353.84 and the out-of-period amount 21.30. The defect is R7's date alone, and I note no uncertainty on it.
